title: Freddie Keppard on violin and picnics with Manuel Perez
summary: Keppard started on violin and took up a horn at picnics; Sidney Bechet's trouble with a train and wine is told.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Sidney Bechet: the man, the horn, the legend

blocks.x: You were speaking about Freddie Kepard earlier. What kind of a style? Was he any different to the other trumpet players? No, no.

He played that Dixieland and jazz trumpet just like the rest of them. Yeah. They all have to play that same way, you see, when you play the trumpet. Because when you get in a band, if you're playing trumpet in a band like they was playing then, you'd have to play that style, you know? The only difference was some fellas could play in brass band music and they couldn't play dance music, you see. That's the two different types of music, you see. When there's a straight and a jazz the other way to dance and music, you got to make a lot of variations and things, you know? So, but he was a good trumpet player, Freddie Kepard. Now he first started with the violin. He started with the violin. I played with him a long time ago when he was playing violin. Oh, yeah. On picnics, yeah. We'd go out and Millenboy can play. Freddie was playing violin then. And when trumpet player put his horn down, Freddie would pick it up, you know, would have intermission. Freddie would pick it up and put it, running over and say, I believe I can play it. And finally he sure did. He got in a horn after he said so he could blow the guy. It wasn't a long time before he started playing good and he got to be famous too. Whose horn was that that he picked up? Some of us, let's see, we had, I believe it was Manuel Perez. Oh, yeah. Manuel Perez, because we playing, I was playing and Manuel Perez was getting all that work out there at Millenboy when Gossum, a fella called Gossum was giving them picnics out there.

Well, I read Piku told us something about playing out there too with Manuel Perez. Oh, yeah, yeah. I played with Piku out there too. Piku said he remembers the same time when Freddie picked up the cornet sometime.
Yeah, yeah. Was it a pic on that same gap with you, Willie?
No, we had, we had, he's dead now. We had a baby, Bayshake, Sidney Bayshake. Oh, yeah.

Sidney Bayshake. Sidney would come on that old smoky, how they call it, that old train, you know, running from up here to Lizzie Field Street. And she'd run all the way back to Millenboy because she was making trips back and forth. Yeah. And Sidney Bayshake, he liked his wine and he'd get too much of that wine and he'd get on there. He'd know he had to play the picnic. He'd get on that train and he'd go to sleep and lay his horn down there, that little clarinet, you know, like a little box, and lay that horn on the seat. And Smoky Mary would run all the way to Millenboy and conducted, well, you know, even just see him sitting there sleeping. We out there at the camp waiting for him and he's sitting up there to train maker all the way back to the city again. And come back, he's still sleeping. So they said, Manny Perez said, anything, you better go out there.
